svg.title: Container and network view
svg.text: Container and network view: everything runs in Docker
New compose project `pipeline-triage` (blue) joins your existing ai-platform-net stack (green). No new host ports except 127.0.0.1:8140.
Windows PC · Docker Desktop (WSL2) · 2× NVIDIA RTX 5080 (2×16 GB VRAM)
docker secrets: Vault role_id + secret_id files
API keys resolved from Vault at start, never baked into images
non-root · read-only rootfs · cap_drop ALL · no-new-privileges
cpu/memory limits · healthchecks · pinned image digests
built in CI, pushed to ai-nexus:5001 as version + sha tags
GitLab reaches the webhook over the Docker network: http://triage-api:8140
MCP servers have no published ports and bind to the internal interface.
How the new containers use the existing stack (numbers match the arrows)
triage-api / triage-worker → redis (Streams + dedup keys), ai-postgres (audit), vault (secrets), minio (evidence).
triage-worker → ollama (chat model + pinned embedding model) over http://ollama:11434.
mcp-* servers → gitlab-server, loki, prometheus, jaeger, ai-sonarqube, trivy-server, ai-nexus, chromadb (read-only).
gitlab-server → triage-api: project webhooks (Pipeline events + Comments) with a secret token.
Existing promtail already ships every container's logs to loki; prometheus gets one new scrape job.
Touch-points on the existing stack (one-time changes, tracked as tasks T0.x)
• ai-postgres: create database `triage` + a dedicated role with a Vault-managed password
• vault: policy + AppRole `pipeline-triage`; secrets under secret/triage/*
• minio: bucket `triage-evidence` with a 14-day lifecycle rule
• ollama: pull the embedding model; set OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2 (shared with Open WebUI)
• prometheus: add a scrape job for triage-api:8140/metrics
• grafana: attach to ai-platform-net (or query by URL) and import the triage dashboard
• gitlab-server: allow webhooks to the local network; create bot user + per-project webhooks
• ai-nexus: create hosted docker repo path devops-ai/* with a deploy role for CI
optional HTTPS egress (only if the provider is enabled)
